_note: Researched 12 Oct 2026. All Budapest casinos are run by LVC Diamond (Las Vegas Casino). Grand Casino and Várkert are closed; Atlantis (XIV) and EuroCenter (III) are open but 5-7 km out, so left off.

items.name: Las Vegas Casino Tropicana
items.priceText: Free entry. Table minimums aren't published. Guides quote about €2–5 per bet. You can play in forints or euros.
items.blurb: The nearest casino that's definitely open: a compact room off Vörösmarty tér. Eight live tables, roulette and blackjack till 4am, slots all night.
items.tip: The door is on Vigadó utca (the postal address says Dorottya utca 2). Bring your actual passport. Only the welcome drink is free.
items.history: The state lottery company bought it in 2011. Since 2015 it has been one of the five Las Vegas Casino rooms in Budapest.
items.entry: 18+, free entry. First visit you're registered and photographed with your ID: UK lads need the original passport, Irish lads their passport. No driving licences. Smart casual, no sportswear or flip-flops. No photos inside.

items.name: Las Vegas Casino Corvin Sétány
items.priceText: Free entry. Minimums aren't published. One listing says tables start at about €2. Most play is cash in forints.
items.blurb: Budapest's biggest casino: 1,200 m², nine live tables and a sea of slots, a short tram ride down the Grand Boulevard.
items.tip: Tram 4 or 6 south down the Grand Boulevard to Corvin-negyed. Reportedly the lowest table minimums in town, so it suits the skint.
items.entry: 18+, free entry. First visit you're registered and photographed with your ID: UK lads need the original passport, Irish lads their passport. No driving licences. Smart casual; security on the door is strict.

items.name: Las Vegas Casino Sofitel
items.priceText: Free entry. Minimums aren't published. A reviewer says roulette can be played in euros or forints. Tea and coffee are charged.
items.hours: Listed as open 24 hours. Live-table hours not confirmed.
items.blurb: The original Las Vegas Casino (1992), right by the Chain Bridge. Roulette with a Danube view, if it's still trading while the hotel is rebuilt.
items.tip: The hotel is being rebuilt as SO/ Budapest, so check Google Maps before you walk over. If it's shut, Tropicana is five minutes away.
items.history: Opened in 1992 in the former Atrium Hyatt, later the Sofitel. Stallone and Schwarzenegger reportedly came to the launch. The hotel closed in December 2020 and is being rebuilt as SO/ Budapest. The 2023 plans kept the casino.
items.entry: 18+, free entry. Expect a slow first check-in: the original passport (no copies), a tablet form and a photo. UK and Irish lads need their passport. No driving licences. Smart casual.

goodToKnow: One company runs every legal casino in Budapest under the Las Vegas Casino brand. Entry is free and 18+. On your first visit they photograph you and your ID, and the law requires this. UK lads need the original passport (since Brexit the UK counts as non-EEA). Irish lads should bring the passport book. Driving licences and photocopies get you turned away. Play is mostly in cash forints, though some central tables take euros, so hit an ATM first and decline the 'convert to GBP/EUR' offer. Drinks are paid for beyond a welcome-drink voucher. Tipping the dealer after a win is normal but not expected. Hungary has banned smoking in enclosed public places since 2012, so expect to smoke outside. Photos are banned inside. There's no cash poker room in the centre: the 'Hold'em' on offer is Ultimate Texas Hold'em against the house.
